title: 06. Typing & Models: TYPING MODULE (Complete)
summary: TYPING MODULE (Complete): explanations and runnable examples.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/typing_complete.py
from typing import (
    # Basic types
    Any, Union, Optional, NoReturn, Never,
    # Generic types
    TypeVar, Generic, ParamSpec, TypeVarTuple,
    # Container types  
    List, Dict, Set, Tuple, FrozenSet, Sequence, Mapping, Iterable,
    # Callable
    Callable, Awaitable, Coroutine,
    # Special
    Literal, Final, TypeAlias, TypeGuard,
    ClassVar, Annotated,
    # Protocols
    Protocol, runtime_checkable, SupportsInt, SupportsFloat,
    # Overload
    overload,
    # Type utilities
    get_type_hints, cast, TYPE_CHECKING,
)

# ============================================================
# PYTHON 3.10+ SIMPLIFIED SYNTAX
# ============================================================
# Old: Union[str, int]    → New: str | int
# Old: Optional[str]      → New: str | None
# Old: List[int]          → New: list[int]
# Old: Dict[str, int]     → New: dict[str, int]
# Old: Tuple[int, ...]    → New: tuple[int, ...]

# --- TypeAlias ---
JSON: TypeAlias = dict[str, "JSON"] | list["JSON"] | str | int | float | bool | None
UserID: TypeAlias = int
Headers: TypeAlias = dict[str, str]

# --- Literal — Restrict to specific values ---
def set_color(color: Literal["red", "green", "blue"]) -> None:
    print(f"Color set to {color}")

# --- Final — Cannot be overridden or reassigned ---
from typing import Final
MAX_RETRIES: Final = 3
# MAX_RETRIES = 5  # Type checker error!

class Base:
    @final
    def critical_method(self):
        """Cannot be overridden in subclasses."""
        pass

# --- Annotated — Attach metadata to types ---
from typing import Annotated

Positive = Annotated[int, "Must be positive"]
Email = Annotated[str, "Must be valid email format"]

def create_user(name: str, age: Positive, email: Email) -> None:
    pass
# Pydantic, FastAPI, and other libraries use Annotated for validation

# --- TypeGuard — Narrow types in conditionals ---
def is_str_list(val: list[object]) -> TypeGuard[list[str]]:
    return all(isinstance(x, str) for x in val)

def process(items: list[object]):
    if is_str_list(items):
        # Type checker knows items is list[str] here
        print(items[0].upper())

# --- ParamSpec (Python 3.10+) — For decorator type hints ---
P = ParamSpec("P")
T = TypeVar("T")

def decorator(func: Callable[P, T]) -> Callable[P, T]:
    @functools.wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> T:
        return func(*args, **kwargs)
    return wrapper

# --- TYPE_CHECKING — Avoid circular imports ---
if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from expensive_module import SomeClass

def process(obj: "SomeClass"):  # String annotation for forward reference
    pass

# --- Overload — Multiple signatures ---
@overload
def get_item(index: int) -> str: ...
@overload
def get_item(index: slice) -> list[str]: ...
def get_item(index):
    if isinstance(index, int):
        return "item"
    return ["item1", "item2"]
```
